comparison: Both strongly support the methodological claims (C1-C5, C36-C46, C58). OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive documentation and internal consistency. Peer reviewers praised the study as 'elegant' with 'carefully and creatively analyzed' data, accepting the reconstruction methodology without concerns. OpenEval includes C28-C29 which peer reviewers address separately in R8.

Both support the measurement precision and correlational findings (C6, C30, C86-C88). OpenEval emphasizes the 99% correlation and consistency with prior work. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these foundational correlations as part of 'convincing' results. Peer R2 also includes C7-C8, C32-C33, C60 which OpenEval addresses in separate results.

OpenEval supports claims C7-C8 about weak/no correlation between neck diameter and head volume at population level. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address these claims but accepted the overall correlational findings. OpenEval also addresses C62 (non-significance) which peers discuss in R13.

OpenEval supports the constant CV finding (C9-C10, C22-C23) as a key result. Peer R3 addresses the paired spine correlation (C13-C18) which OpenEval covers in R5. Both recognize the importance of precision findings, though they group related claims differently. Peer R3 includes C59 which OpenEval groups with R13.

Both strongly support the core experimental finding about paired spine similarity (C13-C18). OpenEval emphasizes the high correlation (slope 0.91, p=0.0002) despite small sample size. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this as 'very important confirmation' of activity-dependent regulation. Peer R3 also includes C22-C23, C59 which OpenEval addresses elsewhere.

Both support the finding that neck length/volume are not correlated between paired spines (C19-C21). OpenEval emphasizes this contrasts with strong correlations for other features. Peer reviewers accepted this without challenge, supporting the interpretation that neck dimensions are not tightly regulated for synaptic strength.

Both support the negative control findings (C24-C27, C93-C95) showing different-dendrite pairs have ~5-fold higher CV and don't differ from random pairings. OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates specificity. Peer reviewers noted this pattern was expected and appropriate, with Reviewer 1 stating it would be surprising if different dendrites showed correlation.

OpenEval supports the information-theoretic analysis (C9-C12, C51, C81, C96-C97) as mathematically sound given assumptions. Peer Reviewer 2 rated this UNCERTAIN, requesting more detail in Results section and discussion of how varying discrimination threshold would affect estimates, indicating the calculation and presentation were unclear.

OpenEval supports the temporal averaging calculations (C52-C56, C82, C98) as appropriate for stated assumptions, noting the binomial model is simplified. Peer Reviewer 3 rated this UNCERTAIN, stating 'I am not sure I quite follow the logic' and noting that high release probability during bursts could remove stochastic noise, indicating confusion about the calculation logic.

Both support the unexpected finding about neck diameter coordination (C61, C63-C64). OpenEval emphasizes the inference of dual control mechanisms is reasonable. Peer reviewers accepted this novel observation without challenge. OpenEval also addresses C62 which peers include in R13.

Both support the exclusion of the triple synapse outlier (C69-C70). OpenEval notes the structural difference provides reasonable grounds for exclusion. Peer reviewers accepted this methodological decision without question. Peer R12 also includes C57 which OpenEval addresses in R13.

Both support the mechanistic connection to CaMKII and synaptic tagging (C71-C74). OpenEval notes the time scales align well with calculated averaging windows but acknowledges speculation about mechanisms. Peer reviewers accepted this mechanistic proposal without challenge, though it remains speculative.

OpenEval supports claims C57-C59 about statistical robustness and comparison to prior work. Peer R12 addresses C57, C69-C70, accepting the comparison to previous work and methodological decisions. Both recognize the importance of contextualizing findings relative to prior studies.

Both support the citations extending findings to other brain regions and species (C65-C67). OpenEval notes the inference about generalizability is appropriately tentative. Peer reviewers accepted these contextualizing citations without question. Peer R14 also includes C68 which OpenEval addresses in R15.

OpenEval supports C68 as providing mechanistic explanation for same-dendrite similarity. Peer R14 addresses C65-C68 together as contextualizing citations. Both accept these as supporting evidence for the main findings and their generalizability.

OpenEval supports C90 showing weak distance effect. Peer Reviewer 3 rated this UNCERTAIN, stating they were 'puzzled' by the no-correlation claim and saw 'a trend towards greater variability as distance increases,' suggesting evidence contradicting the authors' interpretation.

Both support the negative findings for glial and mitochondrial effects (C91-C92). OpenEval notes these rule out anatomical factors as major determinants. Peer reviewers accepted these control analyses without challenge.

OpenEval rates C75-C79 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative proposals about computational advantages lacking direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rated these SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting them as potential functional explanations. This represents a difference in evaluation stringency.

Both support C80 acknowledging CV=0.083 as upper bound on variability. OpenEval also addresses C89 about functional importance. Peer reviewers accepted this limitation acknowledgment as appropriate. Both recognize the importance of stating methodological constraints.

OpenEval supports C99-C100 about short-term plasticity complications, noting they acknowledge important complexities without quantitative resolution. Peer R7 addresses the broader temporal averaging calculation (C52-C56, C82, C98-C100) with UNCERTAIN rating, with Reviewer 3 specifically noting that burst-related high release probability could affect the logic.

OpenEval supports C31-C35, C60, C83-C85 as appropriately cited established knowledge providing context. Peer R2 includes some of these claims (C32-C33, C60) as part of accepted correlational findings. Both recognize the importance of prior literature context.

OpenEval supports methodological choices (C47-C50) including vesicle identification and statistical methods. Peer R8 addresses C28-C29, C47, accepting vesicle methodology as part of 'carefully analyzed' data. Peer R11 addresses C48-C50 with UNCERTAIN rating due to Reviewer 3's concern about ordering spines before correlation analysis potentially inducing artifacts.

OpenEval supports statistical methods (C48-C50) as appropriate. Peer Reviewer 3 raised UNCERTAIN concern that 'ordering spines by size before correlation analysis is inappropriate since it induces a correlation,' suggesting potential statistical artifact. This represents a significant methodological disagreement.
